subject.title: [Feature]: Ticketed read-only standalone MCP App host

question: Should OpenClaw make a Gateway-owned signed view ticket the supported core boundary for standalone and future channel MCP App rendering, and what exact expiry, replay, revocation, and origin guarantees must that ticket enforce?
rationale: This changes the authentication and data-exposure boundary around session-linked MCP App views; source inspection supports the direction, but automation cannot choose the permanent capability semantics or acceptable residual risk.

options.title: Approve scoped view tickets
options.body: Add a narrowly scoped, short-lived, replay-resistant Gateway capability that can read one bound view lease and cannot invoke MCP tools or access other Gateway routes.

options.title: Keep Control UI only
options.body: Retain the authenticated Control UI as the sole MCP Apps host and defer standalone or channel launch surfaces until a different authorization design is approved.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped view tickets
recommendation.body: Add a narrowly scoped, short-lived, replay-resistant Gateway capability that can read one bound view lease and cannot invoke MCP tools or access other Gateway routes.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent MCP and VISION.md history plus co-authorship of the existing Apps host make this the strongest available product and security-boundary routing candidate.
